findings.rule: Titles and abstracts of manuscripts may not contain the positive words: “New”, “Novel”, “First”, “Unprecedented”, or other similar descriptive words, and their adjectives.
The complete postal address and the ORCID iD of the corresponding author should be indicated on the footer of page 1.
findings.problem: The manuscript only provides an email address for the corresponding author; it lacks the complete postal address and ORCID iD.

findings.rule: A list of up to five keywords should be provided below the abstract.
findings.problem: Seven keywords are listed instead of a maximum of five.

findings.rule: A short statement of less than 100 words about the significance of the paper should be added.
findings.problem: The significance statement is approximately 124 words, exceeding the 100-word limit.

findings.rule: At the header on each odd page from page 3, a Running Title not exceeding 50 characters including spaces is required.
findings.problem: The running title 'Coarse-grained elastic network analysis of allosteric coupling in ring ATPases' contains approximately 73 characters, exceeding the 50-character limit.

findings.rule: Introduction, Materials and methods... Conclusion, Conflict of interest, Author contributions, Data availability, (A comment about deposition to a preprint server...), Acknowledgements and References, should be arranged in this order.
findings.problem: The manuscript is missing the 'Conclusion' section entirely. It also lacks a 'Data availability' statement. Additionally, the 'Acknowledgements' section appears after the 'References' section instead of before it.

findings.rule: Do not use vertical lines. Supply a short explanatory title above the body of the table, and table footnotes lettered a, b, c, and so forth, below the body of the table.
findings.problem: Both tables are formatted with ASCII vertical lines. Table 1 footnotes use numbers (1, 2, 3) instead of letters (a, b, c). Titles are placed below or alongside the tables rather than above the body.

findings.rule: All figures must be cited in the text. Number the figures consecutively with Arabic numerals... in the order of their appearance in the text.
findings.problem: Figure 2 is cited before Figure 1 in the Results section, violating the required numerical citation order.

findings.rule: Electronic files of photographs and illustrations should be at 300 dpi resolution... We accept figure files in TIFF, PNG, JPEG or PDF formats.
findings.problem: Figures 1 and 2 are submitted as BMP files (not an accepted format) and at 150 dpi resolution (below the required 300 dpi).

findings.rule: When you submit a figure for the Graphical Abstract, please also upload a short caption less than 100 words about the figure(s).
findings.problem: The graphical abstract caption is approximately 148 words, exceeding the 100-word limit.

findings.rule: All references should be listed in numerical order, starting on a new page, under the heading “References”.
findings.problem: The reference list is not in numerical order; reference [5] appears before [6] and [7], and [7] appears before [6].

findings.rule: The use of “in preparation” and “submitted for publication” is not allowed in the Reference list.
findings.problem: Reference [5] ends with 'In preparation.', which is explicitly prohibited.

findings.rule: References to “unpublished data” and “personal communications” should not appear in the reference list, but appear parenthetically in the text...
findings.problem: Reference [8] lists 'Kuramoto, H. Personal communication, 2025.' instead of placing it parenthetically in the main text.

findings.rule: When referring to macromolecular structures, please use [PDB ID: <PDB ID>] (https://doi.org/10.2210/pdb<PDB ID>/pdb) in the text...
findings.problem: The manuscript cites the structure as '(PDB 6qw9)' instead of using the required format '[PDB ID: 6qw9] (https://doi.org/10.2210/pdb6qw9/pdb)'.
